objective: Write classes with access modifiers, readonly fields, abstract members and implements, and tell private from #private
secondaryObjectives: Derive new types with mapped types, including readonly and optional modifiers

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. 'private and protected are only enforced during type checking', so 'JavaScript runtime constructs like in or simple property lookup can still access' them, making them 'soft private'; JavaScript's # private fields 'remain private after compilation' (hard private); to protect values from malicious actors use closures, WeakMaps or private fields.

Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. Private elements 'cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method'; structuredClone does not clone them. The page does not name JSON.stringify; that JSON.stringify serializes only own enumerable string-keyed properties, and so skips # fields, is the author's statement.

handover: The logs contain no health data; tokens let anyone act as the user until they expire.

scoring.modelReasoning: The token shows up wherever a Session is serialized because TypeScript private is enforced only during type checking; at run time it is an ordinary property, and JSON.stringify includes it. A # private field is private in the running program and is not serialized. toJSON fixes one path but leaves the token visible to spreads and other loggers; protected readonly is still compile-time only.
